summary: Fidelity numeric validation remains executable even after a top-level PolicyInputs metatable guard: validateUnit/validateNonNegative/validateFiniteNonNegative call comparison helpers before establishing type(value) == 'number'. In Luau, equality may invoke __eq even for the same table reference, so a metatable-free PolicyInputs record whose numeric field is a hostile table can execute its __eq inside isFinite/value==value before rejection. nowSeconds reaches isFinite directly and has the same runtime boundary shape. Harden scalar validators to type-check unknown runtime values before equality/comparison/arithmetic; keep the top-level metatable preflight as a separate guard.
evidence: PR #274 head e22c71b7b4f829f1be4c7e9911bdbb2e479a86ab defines isFinite(value: number) as value == value and relational comparisons; validateFiniteNonNegative calls isFinite without a runtime type check.
validateInputs passes distanceStuds/significance/networkRelevance/entityRelevance directly into numeric validators, so a plain top-level record can still carry a metatable-backed non-number scalar.
step passes nowSeconds directly to isFinite before any runtime type assertion, giving the same hostile-scalar path outside PolicyInputs.

MaterialDNA's production validation pattern accepts unknown and checks type(value) == 'number' before calling its isFinite helper, demonstrating the established no-execute boundary shape in this repository.
